name: Bufetat foster care service: fosterhjem.no (Barne-, ungdoms- og familieetaten, the state child, youth and family agency)
coverage: Norway outside Oslo (national entry page for the five regional foster care services; in Oslo the city does this work)
notes: fosterhjem.no leads here; bufdir.no is shared by the directorate (Bufdir) and the agency (Bufetat). The page lists information meetings across the country, online and in person (three were listed for 2 and 3 December 2026), and links to a contact form for each region (rows below). After first contact, people fill in a self-presentation form (egenpresentasjonsskjema), which needs a log-in through ID-porten and Altinn, or a paper copy. Bufetat recruits and trains foster carers; the child welfare service in the child's municipality gives the formal approval.

name: Bufetat and Bufdir: adoption (adopsjon)
coverage: Norway (Bufetat's regional offices assess applicants; Bufdir is the directorate and the appeal body)
notes: The first step is a free preparatory course (adopsjonsforberedende kurs) over two weekends in Lillestrøm, run by Bufetat region øst. People sign up with a form (a Word file) sent through Bufdir's eDialog service or by post. Applications then go by post to the Bufetat region where the applicant lives; they cannot be sent electronically. Bufdir says Adopsjonsforum is the only active adoption organisation and Colombia the only country of origin. Bufetat also runs an advice line for adopted people and adoptive parents.

name: Adopsjonsforum (approved adoption organisation)
coverage: Norway (the only organisation that mediates adoptions from abroad, and only from Colombia, per Bufdir)
notes: Applicants need a confirmation from Adopsjonsforum that it will take their case (formidlingsbekreftelse) before they can join the preparatory course and apply to Bufetat. Bufdir sends readers to Adopsjonsforum for Colombia's requirements and costs. Its own site does not allow automated reading (robots.txt), so its enquiry route was not checked.

name: InorAdopt (formerly an approved adoption organisation)
coverage: Norway (no longer mediates adoptions, per Bufdir)
notes: Bufdir says there were long three approved adoption organisations (Verdens Barn, Adopsjonsforum and InorAdopt) and that only Adopsjonsforum is active now. Its own site does not allow automated reading (robots.txt), so it was not checked.

name: Verdens Barn (formerly an approved adoption organisation)
coverage: Norway (no longer mediates adoptions, per Bufdir)
notes: Bufdir lists Verdens Barn among the three former approved organisations and says only Adopsjonsforum is active now. Search results describe Verdens Barn winding down its adoption work and keeping only support for families who adopted through it (unverified). Its own site does not allow automated reading (robots.txt).

name: Norsk Fosterhjemsforening (Norwegian Foster Care Association)
coverage: Norway (members' association for foster homes, visiting homes and emergency homes, with county branches)
notes: Does not recruit or approve foster carers. It offers members an advice line, peer supporters (likepersoner) and partner lawyers, and runs the annual foster care conference. Its contact page has a general message form. Trondheim, Stavanger and Moss send readers to its pages.

name: Humana omsorg og assistanse: foster care (fosterhjem)
coverage: Norway (regional offices in its Midt, Nord, Sør, Vest and Øst regions; specialised foster homes and emergency homes)
stated_response_time: We will contact you within a short time (innen kort tid)
notes: Private provider. The contact form is for people who want to become a foster, emergency or visiting home; it is drawn by script, so its questions were not read. Its requirements page says Bufetat uses an upper age limit of 67, that people under 25 are approved only as an exception, and that couples should have lived together for at least two years. A history of violence or abuse always rules people out. It also offers a short online test. Not the same company as Humana AS, a medical centre.

name: Stendi: foster care and emergency homes (fosterhjem og beredskapshjem)
coverage: Norway (search results describe specialised foster homes and emergency homes across the country)
notes: Stendi's site showed our reader a bot-check page instead of its content, so this row rests on search results (unverified). They describe a foster home test, digital information meetings, police and health certificates, 4 to 5 meetings to be cleared, a basic course of 2 to 3 days, and pay of 4.3 to 5.8 G for a specialised home with full release from work. Search results place Stendi in the Ambea group.

name: Raus Omsorg: become a foster home (bli fosterhjem)
coverage: Norway (its page says it recruits, assesses and guides foster homes in all of Norway)
notes: Private provider of ordinary, specialised, emergency and respite homes. The contact form asks for name, email, an optional phone number and a message, with a consent box. Its steps are an informal talk, a self-presentation form, home visits with certificates, then approval and follow-up. Its page gives pay of NOK 600,000 to 800,000 a year, agreed individually, plus tax-free expenses at KS rates.

name: Linnea kompetansesenter: reinforced foster homes (forsterkede fosterhjem)
coverage: Vestfold (head office in Tønsberg) and Vestland (office in Bergen)
notes: Private provider founded in 2004. It says it recruits and approves its own foster homes and that all its placements are reinforced: one foster parent stays at home. The contact page, headed 'We are looking for foster homes now - Vestfold and Hordaland', lists recruitment contacts by phone and email (not recorded here). Guidance is weekly at first and never less often than every three weeks.

name: Oslo kommune, Barne- og familieetaten (BFE): Fosterhjem Oslo (the city's foster care service)
coverage: Oslo (recruits foster homes in and around Oslo, up to 2 hours' travel away; does Bufetat's recruitment and training work for Oslo)
stated_response_time: An adviser will contact you as soon as possible (så snart som mulig)
notes: The contact form asks for full name, phone, email and postcode, with a tick to confirm the privacy notice; all fields are required. Oslo also runs information meetings online and in person, gives a phone line and an email address, and has videos in Norwegian, English, Polish, Arabic and Somali. People who want to foster a child they know contact the child welfare service in the district (bydel) where the child lives. The district gives the formal approval.

name: Oslo kommune, Barne- og familieetaten: emergency foster homes (beredskapshjem)
coverage: Oslo (homes in or near Oslo, no more than an hour's drive from the city centre)
notes: A full-time role for one adult, paid at least 4.5 G a year even when no child is placed. Carers choose an age group: 0 to 6, 4 to 12 or 12 to 18. The page asks for a driving licence and a car, a separate room for the child, ideally two adults, and any own children to be of school age or older. It gives a phone line and an email address. The application form's site does not allow automated reading (robots.txt), so its questions were not read.

name: Oslo kommune, Barne- og familieetaten: specialised foster homes (spesialiserte fosterhjem)
coverage: Oslo
notes: For children with complex needs, often instead of an institution. Applicants must first be approved as an ordinary foster home and complete the Solid basic training. One adult is engaged full time on a 5-year agreement; starting pay is 4.7 G without relevant training or 5.2 G with it, plus tax-free expenses at KS rates and 35 days off a year (42 after age 60). The page gives a phone line and an email address.

name: Oslo kommune, Bydel Bjerke: foster and emergency carers (fosterforeldre og beredskapsforeldre)
coverage: Oslo, Bjerke district (its page seeks foster and emergency carers from all of Eastern Norway)
notes: The page invites people to phone one of three lines for an informal talk and names two managers (not recorded here). It lists experience with children, good Norwegian, room for a child, good health and a satisfactory police certificate. Its money examples use 2022 rates, so they are out of date.

name: Bufetat: Fosterhjemstjenesten Nord-Norge (foster care service for northern Norway)
coverage: Nordland, Troms and Finnmark (offices in Hammerfest, Vadsø, Tromsø, Finnsnes, Harstad, Sortland, Bodø and Sandnessjøen)
stated_response_time: An adviser will contact you as soon as possible (så snart som mulig)
notes: The contact form asks for full name, phone, email and postcode, with a tick to confirm the privacy notice; all fields are required. The page says over 150 children and young people in Northern Norway need a new home each year, and lists information meetings and courses. Placed under Finnmark because Bufetat region nord's regional office is in Alta.

name: Bufetat: Fosterhjemstjenesten i Midt-Norge (foster care service for central Norway)
coverage: Trøndelag and Møre og Romsdal (offices in Trondheim, Steinkjer, Molde and Ålesund)
stated_response_time: An adviser will contact you as soon as possible (så snart som mulig)
notes: The contact form asks for full name, phone, email and postcode, with a tick to confirm the privacy notice; all fields are required. It also trains new and existing foster families and has an out-of-hours line for foster carers. An in-person information meeting was listed in Namsos for 2 December 2026.

name: Bufetat: Fosterhjemstjenesten i Rogaland og Vestland (foster care service for western Norway)
coverage: Rogaland and Vestland (offices in Bergen, Førde, Haugesund and Stavanger)
stated_response_time: An adviser will contact you as soon as possible (så snart som mulig)
notes: The contact form asks for full name, phone, email and postcode, with a tick to confirm the privacy notice; all fields are required. Bergen and Stavanger send readers to its digital information meetings. It runs a joint campaign page with Bergen kommune for foster homes in Bergen.

name: Bufetat: Fosterhjemstjenesten, Region øst (foster care service for eastern Norway)
coverage: Innlandet, Akershus and Østfold (offices in Fredrikstad, Lillestrøm, Brumunddal and Lillehammer)
stated_response_time: An adviser will contact you as soon as possible (så snart som mulig)
notes: The contact form asks for full name, phone, email and postcode, with a tick to confirm the privacy notice; all fields are required. The page also gives a phone line with opening hours and an email address. Placed under Akershus, where the Lillestrøm office is; search results describe Lillestrøm as the regional office (unverified). Bufetat region øst also runs the national adoption preparatory courses.

name: Bufetat: Fosterhjemstjenesten i Agder, Vestfold, Telemark og Buskerud (foster care service for southern Norway)
coverage: Agder, Vestfold, Telemark and Buskerud
stated_response_time: An adviser will contact you as soon as possible (så snart som mulig)
notes: The contact form asks for full name, phone, email and postcode, with a tick to confirm the privacy notice; all fields are required. The page lists no office addresses and has an out-of-hours line for foster carers. Search results put Bufetat region sør's regional office in Tønsberg, so the row sits under Vestfold (unverified).

name: Asker kommune: Bli fosterhjem (become a foster home)
coverage: Asker
notes: The child welfare service recruits and approves foster homes itself, so that children can stay in their local area. Its steps are an information meeting, an application form with a written self-presentation, several interviews, talks with any children at home, references, checks with the local NAV office and child welfare service, a health certificate and a full, extended police certificate: usually four to five meetings. The form is drawn by script and was not read. No meeting dates were listed. Its money examples give the basic allowance as NOK 10,847 a month, lower than the figure Bufdir gives from 1 July 2026. Updated 23 September 2026.

name: Bærum kommune: barneverntjenesten, foster homes (Kan du gi et barn gode hverdager?)
coverage: Bærum
notes: Bærum's site refused our reader (HTTP 403), so this row rests on search results (unverified). They show the child welfare service recruiting foster homes itself and offering training, close follow-up and release from work for shorter or longer periods, with a switchboard and an email address for contact.

name: Lillestrøm kommune: Fosterhjem
coverage: Lillestrøm
notes: Information only. It sends people who want to foster to Bufetat and bufdir.no, and lists one named contact (not recorded here).

name: Bergen kommune: Fosterhjem i Bergen (foster homes in Bergen)
coverage: Bergen (child welfare service in four city areas, plus its own foster care guidance unit)
notes: Bufetat recruits and trains foster homes; Bergen follows up the child, the parents and the foster home. The page sends people to Bufetat's digital information meetings and contact form, under the campaign 'Bergens barn - vårt ansvar' (Bergen's children - our responsibility). Each foster home has a fixed contact who visits at least 4 times a year. Updated 2 October 2026.

name: Trondheim kommune: Bli fosterhjem i Trondheim (become a foster home in Trondheim)
coverage: Trondheim
notes: Bufetat recruits and trains foster homes; the municipality's family service approves them and itself recruits homes among relatives and the child's network. Its care unit (Omsorgsenheten) follows up children and carers, with visits at least 4 times a year and a care package for new foster homes. The page sends people to Bufetat and its information meetings and gives a phone line for the care unit. Updated 4 May 2026.

name: Stavanger kommune: Stavanger trenger fosterhjem (Stavanger needs foster homes)
coverage: Stavanger
notes: Sends people to Bufetat's digital information meetings (dates listed up to January 2027) and says to contact Bufetat to start. It gives the basic allowance as equal to the National Insurance basic amount, NOK 136,549 a year, and says released carers get an extra 5 percent of the release pay towards lost pension. Two staff are named with phone and email (not recorded here). Updated 20 November 2026.

name: Kristiansand kommune: Vil du bli støttekontakt, besøkshjem eller fosterhjem? (support contact, visiting home or foster home)
coverage: Kristiansand
notes: One application form (KK066, for people taking on roles for the child welfare service) covers support contacts, visiting homes and foster homes; it is drawn by script and was not read. The foster home section links to Bufetat. A police certificate is needed for every role. Updated 28 May 2026.

name: Drammen kommune: Vil du bli fosterhjem? (Do you want to be a foster home?)
coverage: Drammen
notes: Drammen aims to keep children in the municipality. Its foster care department (27 staff) offers a fixed contact, home visits, family guidance, a trauma-informed care course (TBO-F), networks and respite. Pay follows KS rates, with compensation for occupational pension. Training and assessment take about three months. Two contacts are named with phone and email (not recorded here). Updated 3 September 2026.

name: Fredrikstad kommune: barneverntjenesten, foster homes and other roles
coverage: Fredrikstad and the surrounding area
stated_response_time: We will contact you as soon as we can (Vi kontakter deg så snart vi kan)
notes: The page says there is a serious shortage of foster homes in Fredrikstad and invites families, single people and couples to get in touch. One interest form covers all roles for the child welfare service; it is drawn by script and was not read. Every role needs a police certificate, and roles with overnight stays also need a health certificate. Two staff are named with phone and email (not recorded here).

name: Moss kommune: Vil du være fosterhjem? (foster home, visiting home, activity contact or supervisor)
coverage: Moss
notes: People can phone or email the child welfare intake team, or apply online with an electronic ID. The online form refused our reader (HTTP 403), so its questions were not read. The page sends readers to Bufdir's information meetings and says married, cohabiting and single people and same-sex couples can all be suitable.

name: Bodø kommune: Oppdragstakere for barnevernet (foster homes and other roles for the child welfare service)
coverage: Bodø
notes: One online form ('Søk om å bli fosterhjem') is also used for visiting homes, leisure contacts and supervisors; it refused our reader (HTTP 403), so its questions were not read. The page quotes the general requirements in the foster home regulations and says married, cohabiting, single and same-sex carers, with or without children, in town or country, can foster.

name: Lillehammer kommune: Fosterhjem, besøkshjem og vertsfamilie (foster home, visiting home and host family)
coverage: Lillehammer
notes: People who want to foster a child they know phone the child welfare service. People who want to foster a child they do not know are sent to Bufetat's foster care service, which holds regular information meetings.

name: Sandefjord kommune: Fosterhjem i Sandefjord (foster homes in Sandefjord)
coverage: Sandefjord
notes: Bufetat trains and assesses everyone, with Sandefjord, over about three months. No information meetings were planned when we checked; people can get in touch to register interest. It offers three months of start-up guidance after a child moves in, release from work when needed, family guidance and courses such as TBO-F and Tuning in to Kids.

name: Tønsberg kommune: Fosterhjem (foster homes)
coverage: Tønsberg
notes: Says the municipality needs more foster homes so children can stay local, and links to a Bufetat information meeting on 11 November 2026. Approval is through interviews and home visits. It asks for an extended police certificate, a health certificate, stable finances and housing, the Solid course, and an age between 25 and 60. Two foster care advisers are named with phone and email (not recorded here). Updated 12 October 2026.
